messages:
maya: Quick sync on Optimize toolkit dependencies. Need a cleaned prioritization matrix that maps customer tier -> infra pieces (batching/caching) -> quant pipelines -> eval-alert hooks. I want something we can show Sales and Eng by Monday.

sam: I can take a pass. Should we treat Dedicated customers with an expedited path?

jordan: Recommend two rollout lanes: Enterprise/Dedicated gets full feature set (persistent cache + quant + eval-alerts), Hosted gets batching + ephemeral cache + gradual quant opt-in.

liam: Note: quantization can change model outputs subtly. We need a concordance threshold (we talked about 80%) and an automated rollback if eval drift occurs.

maya: Proposal: gating conditions for rollouts
- telemetry schema (SDK) defined and instrumented
- batching runtime shows >=15% p95 latency improvement on samples
- cache hit-rate >=20% on target flows in smoke tests
- quant concordance >=80% on per-customer eval sets across 3 consecutive runs
- eval-alert false-positive rate <10% in trial window

nina: Question: who owns the telemetry schema and the SDK hooks? We need token-level timings + model_variant metadata to enable cost/routing suggestions.

sam: I'll own telemetry but need eng-runtime help to add trace points. ETA 3 weeks if Runtime gives 1 FTE for sprint.

jordan: I'll add the runtime dependency to the sprint board and draft a minimal SDK test harness. Also adding a short rollback runbook: quant-fallback -> switch to FP32 variant -> notify customers + open incident.

liam: Concordance test harness sketch:
```
input_set: customer_prompt_set_v1
baseline_variant: model-x-fp32
quant_variant: model-x-8bit
metric: semantic_similarity + exact_match for structured outputs
pass_if: concordance >= 0.80 over N=1000 samples
```

maya: Nice. For prioritization I'm thinking ordered work streams: 1) SDK telemetry + event schema 2) batching runtime perf + tests 3) cache prefix store + eviction policy 4) quant pipeline + evaluation infra 5) eval-triggered alert rules + operator playbook.

sam: Agree. Also recommend we surface a quick cost/unit estimate per feature so Sales can explain econ to customers. Even rough numbers per 1M tokens.

jordan: We should also define the MVP acceptance checklist (concise):
- telemetry schema published and test harness passing
- batching shows p95 improvement >=15% on internal synthetic mix
- smoke test cache hit-rate >=20% on interactive flows
- quant concordance >=80% for pilot customers
- one end-to-end eval-alert rule wired to Ops with documented rollback steps

maya: Timeline ask: if telemetry done in 3w, batching + cache work in 4-5w, quant pipeline + eval infra in 6w, then we could start Tier A pilots at ~8w. Is that realistic?

liam: Roughly yes. Major blocker is runtime FTEs and a partner for labeled prompt sets for concordance checks.

nina: I'll reach out to Solutions Eng and Customer Success for pilot prompt sets and customer opt-ins.
